Hi, it looks like your reply didn't come through. My Bosch WAN28281GB stopped part way through a wash and is showing E18, with water still in the drum. What does that mean?

Sorry about that. Your previous message got an error instead of an answer.

E18 on a Bosch washing machine means a drainage fault. The machine tried to pump the water out but couldn't within the expected time, so it stopped. The most common cause is a blocked pump filter, which is usually easy to fix yourself.

Common causes
• Blocked pump filter (coins, hair grips, fluff, small socks, bra wires)
• Kinked or squashed drain hose behind the machine
• Blocked sink trap or standpipe where the hose drains
• Faulty drain pump (less common)

How to fix it

1. Switch off and unplug the machine. If it was a hot wash, let the water cool first.
2. Prepare for water. Put towels down and get a shallow tray or baking dish. There could be several litres, so expect to empty it a few times.
3. Open the small service flap at the bottom corner of the front panel.
4. Use the emergency drain hose, a small tube next to the filter. Pull it out, hold it over your tray, remove its cap, and let the water drain. Re-cap it whenever you need to empty the tray.
5. Remove the pump filter once the water has stopped. Unscrew it anticlockwise slowly, as a bit more water will come out. Clear any debris and rinse it.
6. Check the impeller. Look into the opening behind the filter and make sure the small impeller turns freely and nothing is stuck in it.
7. Refit the filter firmly (clockwise until tight) and recap the emergency hose so it won't leak.
8. Check the drain hose behind the machine for kinks, and make sure the sink trap or standpipe it drains into isn't blocked.
9. Plug back in and run a Rinse/Spin or Drain programme to test it. Switching off and on again should clear the error.

The door will stay locked while there's water in the drum, so don't force it. It should release once the water is drained.

If E18 comes back
• If you hear the pump humming but no water moves, there may still be a blockage, or the pump may be seized.
• If you hear nothing at all when it should be draining, the pump or its wiring may have failed.

In either case it's worth contacting Bosch customer service or a local appliance engineer. A replacement drain pump is a fairly common and inexpensive repair.

Thanks, I've worked through those steps. I emptied the water with the emergency hose (took several trays, it was grey and smelled a bit). The filter had a child's sock and a hair grip wrapped round it, plus lots of fluff. The impeller was slightly notchy then turned freely, and the drain hose and sink both look fine. I ran a rinse and spin afterwards and it drained quickly, E18 has gone and it spins normally. There's no burning smell and no water near the socket, though the floor got a little wet while I was draining the filter. Is there anything else I should do?

Great job. A sock and hair grip wrapped round the filter is a classic cause of E18, and a quick drain on the rinse and spin suggests it's fixed.

Worth doing now
• Dry the floor and the area under the service flap fully, including any water that ran under the machine. This makes it easier to spot any new leak.
• Check for drips during the next wash. Glance at the filter flap partway through. If it's damp, the filter may not be screwed in fully or the emergency hose cap may be loose.
• Run a maintenance wash to clear the smell. Use an empty machine on the hottest cotton cycle (90°C if available) with a washing machine cleaner, or a scoop of soda crystals or bio powder. Grey, smelly water usually means a build-up of detergent residue and grime.
• Wipe the door seal, especially inside the folds, and clean the detergent drawer. Both often harbour residue that adds to the smell.

To prevent it happening again
• Use a mesh laundry bag for small items like children's socks, and bras with wires.
• Check pockets for hair grips, coins and tissues.
• Clean the pump filter every 2 to 3 months, or sooner if you notice slow draining.
• Do a hot maintenance wash monthly if you mostly wash at low temperatures.
• Leave the door and drawer ajar between washes to let them dry out.

Keep an eye on the pump
The initial notchiness was probably just the debris. Watch for:
• A grinding, rattling or loud humming noise when draining
• Slow draining or E18 returning even with a clean filter

If either happens, the pump may be worn and need replacing, which is a fairly common and inexpensive repair.

Also, my earlier message got cut off. The missing point was this: if E18 returns and you hear no pump sound at all when it should be draining, that points to a failed pump or an electrical or wiring fault. That's a job for a Bosch engineer or qualified repairer rather than DIY.
